title: Incident Communications, Status Page & Customer Comms Templates
author: Emily Chen
body:
Purpose
This page centralizes our incident communications playbook: how we notify internal stakeholders, update the public status page, and communicate with affected customers. It contains standard templates for initial acknowledgements, status updates, and post-incident follow-ups, plus guidance for runbook owners and on-call rotations.

Scope
- Applies to all production incidents that affect customer-facing services (hosted API, Dedicated control plane, Redwood Console).
- Includes: incident triage notifications, status page updates, customer-facing emails/Slack templates, press-sensitive escalations (see Security/Legal).

Ownership and roles
- Incident Commander (IC): leads triage and public messaging until handoff.
- Communications Lead: owns status page and customer comms. Usually Customer Success or on-call engineering designee for major incidents.
- On-call Engineer(s): owns mitigation steps and technical updates.
- SRE Manager / Pager Escalation: secondary escalation for capacity/infra incidents.
- Legal / Security / PR: looped in for incidents with data exposure or regulatory impact.

Incident severity levels and paging thresholds (examples)
1) Sev0 (P1) 

System-wide outage
   - Symptoms: API 5xx rate > 40% across regions, > 95% token generation failures, or control plane unavailable.
   - Page immediately: primary on-call + IC + SRE Manager + Communications.
   - SLA impact: severe, notify leadership and Customer Success.
2) Sev1 (P2) 

Major degradation
   - Symptoms: sustained 5xx > 10% for > 5 minutes, median latency > 5x baseline on top-tier endpoints, or major capacity degradation affecting customers.
   - Page primary on-call and IC. Communications notified for public update within 15 minutes.
3) Sev2 (P3) 

Partial degradation/feature regression
   - Symptoms: elevated errors for a subset of customers/routes, non-critical functionality impacted.
   - Triage by on-call; Communications not required unless customer impact reported.

Paging & escalation steps

1) Detection: alert fired from monitoring, customer report, or internal automation.
2) Acknowledge: on-call must acknowledge in the pager within 5 minutes. If not acknowledged, the pager escalates per rotation policy.
3) Owner assignment: IC assigned (by pager escalation rules or first responder).
4) Communicate: Communications Lead publishes an initial status page entry (see templates) within 15 minutes for Sev0/Sev1.
5) Mitigate: on-call follows runbook for impacted service.
6) Update cadence: every 15 minutes for Sev0, every 30 minutes for Sev1 until stabilization.
7) Resolution & close: confirm fix, monitor for 60 minutes, close alert, and open postmortem if required.

Runbook requirements and links
- Every production service must have a runbook with: owner, runbook steps for common alerts, rollback steps, mitigation commands, telemetry dashboards, and postmortem checklist.
- Runbook owners must run a tabletop/game day exercise annually.
- Reference runbooks: (link to service-specific runbooks should be maintained in the runbook index).

Quick runbook example (public-apis-deployment)
1) Symptoms:
   - API 5xx spike >10% for 3 consecutive 1m windows
2) Immediate checks:
   - kubectl get pods -n public-apis | grep CrashLoopBackOff
   - aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --metric-name Latency --namespace Redwood/NGW ...
   - Check deployment events: kubectl describe deploy public-api
3) Mitigations:
   - Scale up replica count: kubectl scale deploy public-api --replicas=5
   - Roll back last deployment: kubectl rollout undo deploy/public-api
   - Fallback routing: enable region fallback policy via routing service CLI
4) Post-incident: capture timestamps, actions, and affected customers in incident page.

Postmortem policy and template
- Postmortem required for Sev0 and Sev1 incidents that consume > 25% of an error budget or affect > 5% of active customers.
- Timeline: postmortem draft within 72 hours; final postmortem published and reviewed in 14 days.

Postmortem template (to paste into a new Confluence page)
1) Title: [SEV#] Service - Short description - YYYY-MM-DD
2) Owner: Who wrote this
3) Incident timeline: chronological bullet list with UTC timestamps
4) Impact: affected services, regions, customer segments, error budget impact
5) Root cause: short explanation
6) Resolution & mitigation: what fixed it in production
7) Action items: short-lived (owner, ETA), long-term (owner, ETA)
8) Detection & alerting notes: what fired, what didn't
9) Communications & customer impact: links to status and customer emails
10) Lessons learned and follow-up game day schedule

On-call rotations and expectations
- Primary on-call rotation: 1-week rotation, Monday 08:00 UTC to next Monday 08:00 UTC.
- Secondary/backup on-call: provides escalation if primary unresponsive.
- Shift handoff: outgoing on-call posts a brief handoff note in #oncall-handoffs Slack channel with ongoing incidents and unstable services.
- Time commitments: expected average of 3-5 pages per week; if a user exceeds 2 consecutive weeks with >5 pages/week, review rotation load.

Game days and tabletop exercises
- Frequency: team-level game days quarterly; company-wide scenarios annually.
- Objectives: validate runbooks, verify paging/escallation flows, exercise customer comms and status page updates.
- Typical agenda:
  1) Pre-brief (15m): objectives and scope
  2) Injects (1h): simulated alerts and customer reports
  3) Triage & mitigation (1h): live exercise following runbooks
  4) Communications (30m): update status page and send simulated customer emails
  5) Debrief (30m): capture action items and owners

Status page guidelines and templates
- Use our status.redwood.ai status page service. Communications Lead updates the public page for any incident impacting availability or latency beyond thresholds.
- Minimum public update cadence: within 15 minutes of detection for Sev0/Sev1, then every 30 minutes until resolved.
- Status page fields to populate: Title, Impact, Affected services, Region, Start time (UTC), Current status, Next update ETA, Mitigation in progress, Links to system metrics and customer contact.

Status page template (initial)
- Title: "Partial outage impacting [service-name]"
- Impact: "Customers may experience increased errors and timeouts when calling [endpoint(s)]. This is affecting ~X% of requests."
- Affected services: "Hosted API (us-west-2), Redwood Console"
- Start time: "2026-02-18T14:12:00Z"
- Current status: "Investigating"
- Next update: "in 15 minutes"
- Mitigation: "On-call team scaling replicas and evaluating recent deployment."

Status page template (update)
- Title: "Update: [service-name]"
- Summary: "We have identified a likely cause and are applying mitigations. Error rates reduced from X% to Y%."
- Affected services: as above
- Next update: "in 30 minutes"

Status page template (resolved)
- Title: "Resolved: [service-name]"
- Summary: "Service restored. Root cause investigation underway; postmortem will be published within 14 days."
- Impact: "Total downtime ~ XX minutes. Affected customers may have seen errors during this window."

Customer communication templates
1) Initial acknowledgement (send within 15 minutes for Sev0/Sev1)
Subject: "Redwood status: we are investigating an issue affecting [service]"
Body:
Hello {CustomerName},

We’re aware of increased errors and degraded performance impacting {service} starting at {start_time_utc}. Our on-call engineers are investigating. We will provide an update within 15 minutes.

Impact: {short impact summary}
Mitigation: {short mitigation steps underway}

We apologize for the disruption. If you rely on safety-critical functionality or have SLAs that may be impacted, reply to this message and we will prioritize a direct update.

– Redwood Inference Support Team

2) Follow-up update (periodic)
Subject: "Redwood status update: [service] – {short summary}"
Body:
Hello {CustomerName},

Update on the incident affecting {service}: {summary of progress, e.g., error rate reduced from X% to Y%, mitigation steps taken}. Estimated next update: {ETA}.

If you’re seeing continued issues, please reply and include request IDs or timestamps to help our investigation.

– Communications Lead, Redwood Inference

3) Resolution and RCA commitment
Subject: "Redwood resolved: [service] incident on {date} — postmortem forthcoming"
Body:
Hello {CustomerName},

The incident affecting {service} has been resolved as of {resolved_time_utc}. We are publishing a postmortem and action plan within 14 days. Key points:
- Impact: what customers experienced (short bullets)
- What fixed it: short summary
- Next steps: list of action items and ETA

If you’d like a dedicated briefing, reply and we’ll schedule time with the engineering and Customer Success teams.

– Redwood Inference Support Team

Press and legal-sensitive communications
- Escalate to Legal and PR immediately for any incident involving customer data exposure, regulatory scope (GDPR/CCPA), or broader reputational impact.
- Communications Lead should not publish a customer-facing statement without Legal sign-off in these cases.

Templates for internal Slack updates
- Initial pager channel message (short): "[SEV#] [service-name] - Investigating increased 5xx rates. IC: @oncall. Status page: [link]"
- Public Slack update (customer-facing channels): "Update: We are aware of issues with [service]. We’ve published a status page update: [link]."

Post-incident follow-up checklist
- Create incident page and paste timeline, metrics, and commands run.
- Draft postmortem within 72 hours.
- Assign action items and track in the engineering backlog.
- Schedule retrospective and game day within 30 days for high-impact incidents.

Appendix: useful commands and links
- Status page editor CLI: redwood status update --id <inc-id> --state investigating --message "Scaling replicas"
- Pager escalation matrix: (link to pagerduty schedule)
- Runbook index: (link to runbook index)
- Contact list: oncall@redwood.ai, support@redwood.ai, security@redwood.ai
